capability_targets.what_it_does: Redash has no open self-service signup -- accounts after the first are created by an admin invite. The one real self-service account-creation flow is the first-run '/setup' wizard, which creates the organisation and its first (admin) user. Used as the closest real equivalent; see 'unresolved'.
Authenticate an existing user with email/password
Register a new data source (connection) an org can run queries against
Create a query against a data source and execute it
Turn a query's result set into a chart/table visualisation
Pin a visualisation onto a shared dashboard as a widget
Issue a public link (API-key-backed) so a dashboard can be viewed without logging in

harvest_source.structural_match: Connect a data source, write a query against it, turn the result into a visualisation, pin visualisations onto a shared dashboard, and give other people a link -- the same connect/query/chart/share shape as Metabase, minus the hosted infrastructure. Verified live: DataSourceListResource (data_sources.py) creates a data source, QueryListResource (queries.py) creates and runs a query on it, VisualizationListResource (visualizations.py) turns the result into a chart, WidgetListResource (widgets.py) pins it onto a dashboard, DashboardShareResource (dashboards.py) issues the public link.

capabilities.what_it_does: First-run setup wizard: creates the Organization, its two built-in Groups (admin/default) and the first User (the org admin), then logs that user in. This is Redash's only self-service account-creation route -- every subsequent user is created by an admin invite (see UserInviteResource, not harvested here), not by open signup.

security_constraints.guard: redirects to / if an organisation already exists and MULTI_ORG is off -- this route only ever runs once per instance

side_effects: creates a User row and hashes its password

capabilities.what_it_does: Authenticates a user by email/password against the current organisation and starts a Flask-Login session; on success redirects to the page that triggered the login.
Ends the current Flask-Login session and redirects to the login URL.
Registers a new DataSource (a connection configuration such as a PostgreSQL/MySQL/etc connection string) that queries can subsequently be run against, and assigns it to the default group.

side_effects: creates a DataSourceGroup row for the default group

capabilities.what_it_does: Creates a new Query row against a named data source (query text plus options) and triggers execution, returning the serialized query with its latest result once available.

side_effects: triggers execution against the data source and attaches the latest QueryResult

capabilities.what_it_does: Attaches a new Visualization (chart type, options) to an existing query's result set.
Pins a visualisation (or a text box) onto a dashboard by creating a Widget row that references both the dashboard and the visualisation.
Enables anonymous public access to a dashboard by creating (or reusing) an ApiKey tied to it, and returns the public URL built from that key.

side_effects: creates or reuses an ApiKey row for the dashboard

unresolved: register account -- Redash ships no open public self-registration route. Accounts after the first are created by an admin sending an invite (UserInviteResource, POST /api/users, admin-only -- not the person creating their own account) or via SSO/SAML/LDAP if configured. The one route a person drives to create the first account of their own is the '/setup' wizard (redash/handlers/setup.py:setup), which also creates the Organization itself, and only runs once (it redirects to / if an org already exists and MULTI_ORG is off). Used here as the closest real equivalent to 'register account' rather than inventing an open-signup endpoint that does not exist in this codebase.

view_adapter -- left blank. Unlike Indico (which ships indico.web.flask.util:make_view_func as a real, reusable, already-existing 'RH class -> Flask view' bridge used throughout its own blueprint registration), neither Redash's own source nor Flask-RESTful exposes an equivalent standalone 'resource class -> view function' function at module scope. Flask-RESTful's Api.add_resource calls resource.as_view(...) internally inside the library's own Api class, not as a separately importable single-argument function; Redash's own ApiExt.add_org_resource (redash/handlers/api.py) just delegates straight into that same internal call. No genuinely existing symbol of the shape host.py's RUNTIME_ADAPTER_FIELD needs -- 'module.path:callable' taking one class argument and returning a view function -- was found in Redash's own code, so per the spec ('do not guess them... leave it empty, run anyway, record what the host said') it is left blank rather than invented. Expected consequence, to be confirmed by the actual host.py --check / host_test run: log in / log out / register account (plain functions, not classes) will not resolve to a class at all and fail to bind ('part has no class named by ...'); the five Flask-RESTful Resource-class capabilities will resolve to a class but, with no adapter, be bound as the raw class object rather than a proper view -- whether that serves a real response or errors at request time is exactly what the run will show.

models_loader -- left blank. redash.app:create_app itself does 'from .models import db, users' and calls handlers.init_app(app) inline, so every model and every route is already registered by the time create_app() returns -- there is no separate lazy model-registration step the way Indico's import_all_models() was needed for SQLAlchemy mapper resolution.

data_filename / data_shape.data_access -- left blank on every capability, same reasoning as the event-ticketing form: Redash's real persistence is PostgreSQL via SQLAlchemy models (DataSource, Query, Visualization, Widget, Dashboard, User, Organization -- real tables), not a flat JSON file per entity. The real table/model is named in provenance.source_symbol and what_it_does instead.

shared_lib_calls -- left empty on every capability. Redash implements its own session (Flask-Login), password hashing (User.hash_password) and its own API-key mechanism (ApiKey model) -- none of it calls CAP-0000's shared library. Asserting an integration that is not in the code would be inventing one.

run.start_command / run.port / run.health_endpoint -- taken from Redash's own bin/run and manage.py runserver command and its documented default port (5000); not run live this session, recorded for completeness of the form's 'run' block, same as it would be needed for a from-scratch process launch outside of host.py (which builds and drives the app in-process rather than shelling out to this command).
